note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings, and in designated no-passing zones.

question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:
options: a:Anything makes road conditions less than perfect (wet, slippery, poor visibility).;b:You see a police car only.;c:You are entering a highway with other cars.;d:Traffic is flowing faster than the limit.
note: Reduce your speed below the posted limit whenever conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make driving less than ideal.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to create distance.,b:Stop immediately in your lane.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,d:Maintain your speed and lane.
note: Pull over or otherwise clear the path for emergency vehicles so they can reach their destination quickly and safely.

question: If involved in a crash, what should a driver do at the scene?
options: a:Stop at or near the scene and move out of traffic if possible.,b:Stand or walk in traffic lanes to direct cars.,c:Leave without leaving information.,d:Drive away slowly and report later.
note: Stop and secure the scene; avoid standing in traffic lanes and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before and after passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Sound your horn three times.,c:Move back into the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots and signal; re-enter your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.,d:Blue.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; yellow separates opposite directions.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,b:Look for a way around lowered gates.,c:Drive faster than the train.,d:Ignore it if no train is visible.
note: Railroad warning signs alert you to the possible presence of trains; be prepared to stop and obey crossing devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross those lines?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or from a private road, driveway, or alley.,b:To pass slower traffic when safe.,c:Whenever traffic ahead is moving slowly.,d:To pass bicyclists at any time.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; crossing is allowed only to make left turns into driveways, alleys, or private roads.

question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn up the radio to listen for an approaching train.,c:Assume trains will always stop for vehicles.,d:Drive quickly across to minimize time on the tracks.
note: If there are no active warnings, look and listen carefully in both directions and cross only when clear.

question: Is it legal to consume alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Yes, if you are not driving.,b:Yes, if riding in the back seat.,c:No — it's illegal to consume or possess open containers on public roads.,d:Yes, only in pickup truck beds.
note: Possessing or consuming open alcoholic beverages in areas of a vehicle normally occupied by driver or passengers on public roads is prohibited.

question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,b:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.,c:Merge to the right and continue.,d:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield, and go only when the intersection is clear and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Slow down, cover the brake, look left-right-left, and be prepared to yield—yielding to vehicles from the right.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking.,c:Stop in the center of the road and wait for others to pass.,d:Only yield if you see a stop sign.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection take your foot off the accelerator, cover the brake, look left-right-left, and yield to vehicles from the right as necessary.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Know how any medicines affect your driving, keep fit, and drive within your limitations.;b:Only drive when perfectly healthy with no medications ever.;c:Ignore minor physical issues and drive anyway.;d:Rely on passengers to handle driving if you feel unwell.
note: Be aware of how medications affect you, maintain fitness, have medical checks as needed, and drive within your physical capabilities.

question: What is the only effective method to lower your BAC?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to remove the alcohol.
note: The only way to lower BAC is to allow time for the body to metabolize the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway you should:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.;b:Drive quickly to merge with traffic.;c:Stop with part of your car in the roadway to warn others.;d:Blow your horn to alert traffic.
note: Yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from a private road or driveway—do not force your way into traffic.

question: Which in-vehicle distraction most increases crash risk?
options: a:Using a cell phone, including hands-free calls.,b:Playing the radio at moderate volume.,c:Using a CD player to change tracks occasionally.,d:Adjusting the seat before driving.
note: Cell phone use, even hands-free, significantly distracts drivers and raises crash risk.

question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only the passage of time.,b:Hot coffee and fresh air.,c:Tomato juice and lime.,d:Exercising vigorously.
note: Only time will reduce the blood alcohol content; remedies like coffee or fresh air do not speed up alcohol metabolism.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Slow down and continue driving.,b:Drive with your flashers on.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: Upon hearing an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What is the proper method to check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Look into the rearview mirror.,c:Look into the side mirror only.,d:Use your peripheral vision without turning your head.
note: To confirm no vehicle is in your blind spot, physically turn and look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter.

question: Which factor does vehicle stopping distance NOT depend on?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The condition of your brakes.,d:The road surface and weather.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brakes, tires, roadway conditions, and speed; it does not depend on the time of day.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning, you should:
options: a:Use your signal several seconds before making the turn.;b:Increase your speed to create a gap.;c:Turn the wheel abruptly without signaling.;d:Honk to warn other drivers before turning.
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before turning to give other road users time to react.

question: On average, how much alcohol does the human body eliminate per hour?
options: a:About one standard drink per hour.,b:About three drinks per hour.,c:About two drinks per hour.,d:None; alcohol is eliminated instantly.
note: The average person metabolizes roughly one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect this rate.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Get out of the car and walk for help.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Lay down in the car and sleep.,d:Stand on the road to signal other drivers.
note: Remain in your vehicle, run the engine sparingly for heat, and wait for rescue; you're easier to find in the car.

question: If you begin feeling drowsy while driving, the safest choice is to:
options: a:Open a window to get fresh air.;b:Stop driving and rest.;c:Drink coffee and continue driving.;d:Turn up the radio and keep going.
note: Fatigue poses a serious risk similar to impairment from alcohol. If you feel tired while driving, stop and rest rather than trying short-term fixes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection while lights are working, you should:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the officer rather than the traffic signals.;b:Follow the traffic light over the officer's instructions.;c:Honk to hurry the officer.;d:Ignore both and proceed with caution.
note: An officer's directions override traffic signals and must be followed to ensure orderly traffic flow and safety.

question: Approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign and come to a complete stop.;b:Continue through if no other traffic is present.;c:Increase speed to clear the intersection quickly.;d:Wait for a police officer to direct traffic.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and then proceeding when the way is clear, the same as a stop sign.

question: When driving at night and another vehicle approaches, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Low beams.,c:Parking lights only.,d:No lights.
note: Use low-beam headlights when approaching or following other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane, what actions should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer to the right, and brake.;b:Blow your horn, steer left, and accelerate.;c:Slow down and maintain course, hoping they correct their path.;d:Stop immediately and open your door.
note: If a vehicle is in your lane, honk to attract attention, steer right to avoid a head-on collision, and brake firmly; avoid swerving left into oncoming traffic.

question: What should you do first if you must slow on a slippery surface?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply the parking brake.
note: On slippery roads, first ease off the accelerator to slow down gradually; if necessary, apply brakes gently and progressively.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color and how should drivers treat them?
options: a:White and they must always be obeyed.,b:Blue and they are optional.,c:Green and they are only suggestions.,d:Yellow and they warn of hazards.
note: Regulatory signs typically have a white background with black markings and convey rules that drivers must obey.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to cross solid yellow center lines?
options: a:Only to make a left turn into or from a private road, driveway, or alley.,b:At any time to pass slower traffic.,c:Only during daylight hours.,d:To pass another vehicle on a hill.
note: Solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; you may cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?
options: a:You must use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic to complete the pass when it is safe and legal.,b:Never cross the centerline to pass.,c:Use the shoulder to pass when it is clear.,d:Flash your lights to tell the other vehicle to speed up.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road normally requires moving into the oncoming traffic lane; only pass when it is safe and legal.

question: On slick roads, you should:
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual and avoid abrupt maneuvers.;b:Accelerate quickly to maintain control.;c:Change lanes rapidly to avoid hazards.;d:Drive the same as on dry roads.
note: Slow down and take turns more cautiously on slippery roads to reduce the risk of skidding.

question: Any activity that requires you to do which of these could lead to a crash?
options: a:Take your eyes off the road,b:Take your hands off the wheel,c:Take your attention away from driving.
note: Distractions that take your eyes off the road, hands off the wheel, or attention away from driving increase the risk of a crash.

question: What is the correct top-to-bottom order for vertically arranged traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.;b:Green, yellow, red.;c:Yellow, red, green.;d:Red, green, yellow.
note: On vertical traffic signals, red is at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom; horizontally, red is always on the left.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail while the signals warn of an approaching train.,b:Slow down and proceed if you do not see a train.,c:Speed through if you can clear the tracks quickly.,d:Cross and then look back for trains.
note: If warning lights are flashing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until it is safe to cross.

question: What's the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Slow down when roads are wet and avoid standing water; keep tires properly maintained.;b:Use cruise control to stabilize speed.;c:Drive faster to pass over water quickly.;d:Inflate tires beyond recommended pressure to shed water.
note: Reduce speed in wet conditions, avoid standing water, and ensure tires are in good condition to lower hydroplaning risk.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with care.,c:Continue through at normal speed.,d:Yield only to pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow indicates you should slow down, look, and proceed with caution.

question: What best ensures safety when you back your vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind and check for obstacles before getting into the driver's seat.;b:Rely solely on rearview mirrors and backup camera.;c:Honk continuously while reversing.;d:Back rapidly to finish quickly.
note: Because visibility behind the vehicle is limited, walk to the rear to check for children or objects before backing.

question: When executing a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,b:Increase your speed to complete the turn sooner.,c:Maintain the same speed you had before turning.,d:Vary your speed randomly during the turn.
note: When turning, slow to a speed that lets you maintain control, stay within your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, which actions are required?
options: a:Stop, determine if anyone is injured, and call the police if necessary.;b:Continue driving if damage appears minor.;c:Only move the vehicles and do not call the police.;d:Report the crash only if you feel at fault.
note: Stop your vehicle, check for injuries, call emergency services when needed, and report crashes to law enforcement when there is injury, death, or significant property damage.

question: If you are in the right lane of a multi-lane highway and want to move left, what should you do?
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Signal and change lanes without checking mirrors.,c:Only check your side mirror and then move left.,d:Accelerate and move left quickly.
note: Always check mirrors, signal, and glance over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: Which document must the driver present when stopped for a violation or equipment check?
options: a:Proof of insurance.,b:Driver's license.,c:Proof of vehicle registration.
note: When stopped, a driver must present their license; they should also have registration and proof of insurance available in the vehicle.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Do not step into a street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching closely.,b:Always insist on your right-of-way no matter vehicle distance.,c:Cross at any point because drivers must stop.,d:Walk against traffic on sidewalks for safety.
note: Even though pedestrians have rights in crosswalks, do not enter the roadway if an approaching vehicle is too close to safely stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is passing prohibited?
options: a:At an intersection, on a hill or curve, and when school bus lights are flashing.;b:Only when a no-passing sign is posted.;c:Only when daytime visibility is poor.;d:Only on highways with multiple lanes.
note: Do not pass on hills, curves, intersections, railroad crossings, or when a school bus has flashing red lights, or in other marked no-passing zones.

question: A work zone may be:
options: a:Stationary or moving and is marked with orange signs; drivers must slow down and pay extra attention.;b:Marked only with black and white signs.;c:Ignored if you are in a hurry.;d:Restricted to times of road construction only.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., mowing) and are marked with orange signs—reduce speed and be alert.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving at the same speed.,d:Turn off your headlights immediately.
note: Grip the wheel, gradually reduce speed by easing off the gas, then brake lightly and pull to a safe area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should first:
options: a:Turn on your headlights.;b:Reduce your speed by half.;c:Check your rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.;d:Sound your horn to warn others.
note: Always check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to ensure no vehicle is in your blind spot before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a location where parking is prohibited?
options: a:Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.,b:Within 20 feet of a fire hydrant.,c:Within 200 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.,d:In a private driveway with permission.
note: Parking is prohibited within 15 feet of a fire hydrant; other restrictions include within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection and within 50 feet of a railroad crossing rail.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing lanes is a ____ line.
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Broken white.,c:Solid yellow.,d:Solid white.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:When in a construction zone only.,c:Only in rural areas.,d:When you're tired.
note: Driving so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow can be illegal and hazardous.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is correct?
options: a:You should slow down in rain and fog.;b:You can drive the same as in clear weather.;c:You should increase your speed in rain to pass quickly.;d:You should ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.
note: When weather changes, adjust your driving—slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you that may not be adapting.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.,d:You have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution — slow down and proceed carefully when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to come to a complete stop?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A yellow arrow.,d:A steady green light.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, then proceed when safe.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who fails to obey traffic laws?
options: a:They can be ticketed.,b:They are always correct because they are more vulnerable.,c:They will always receive just a warning from law enforcement.,d:They cannot be stopped by police.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicle drivers and may be ticketed for violations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway from an on-ramp, the best practice is to:
options: a:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge safely.;b:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening at a much lower speed.;c:Turn on hazard lights until fully merged.;d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed so you can blend with traffic; vehicles on the freeway have the right-of-way.

question: On roads with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:The side facing oncoming traffic (so they can see approaching vehicles).,b:The same side as traffic movement.,c:The side with the heaviest traffic.,d:The middle of the road for visibility.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic when sidewalks are not available so they can see approaching vehicles.

question: How should you respond when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait.,c:Increase your speed to clear the area quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; you should slow down and proceed carefully without stopping unless necessary.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Do not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and administer first aid as appropriate until help arrives.,b:Always move injured people to the nearest sidewalk immediately.,c:Leave the injured and seek help elsewhere.,d:Forcefully reposition injured limbs to reduce pain.
note: Avoid moving injured persons unless their life is in danger from immediate hazards; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.

question: Which measure may help drivers conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down and decelerating gradually rather than frequent hard braking.,b:Accelerating quickly whenever possible.,c:Idling the engine while parked to warm the car.,d:Driving with lower tire pressure than recommended.
note: Anticipating traffic and slowing gradually reduces unnecessary acceleration and improves fuel economy.

question: What effect can result from combining alcohol with drugs?
options: a:Decrease combined effects.,b:Increase the effects of both.,c:Help cure your illness.
note: Combining alcohol and drugs can amplify impairing effects, making driving even more dangerous.

question: What is the most common color of warning signs?
options: a:Yellow.;b:Red.;c:Green.;d:Blue.
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings to warn drivers about upcoming conditions.

question: What hazard can a leaking exhaust system create for vehicle occupants?
options: a:It can make you drowsy or cause death from toxic fumes.,b:It causes excessive oil consumption.,c:It forces you to have tune-ups more often.
note: A leaky exhaust can let carbon monoxide and other toxic gases enter the vehicle, causing drowsiness, unconsciousness, or death in a short time.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is affected by all of the following EXCEPT:
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:Your body weight.,c:How much alcohol you consume.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC depends on the amount of alcohol consumed, the time between drinks, and body weight; the type of drink (beer, wine, liquor) does not change the alcohol content absorbed by the body per unit of alcohol consumed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are out at an intersection due to a power outage, you should:
options: a:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop and yield to others appropriately.;b:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed without stopping.;c:Park and wait for power to be restored.;d:Use hand signals to direct other vehicles.
note: When signals are out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop—stop, then proceed when it's your turn and the way is clear.

question: An advisory speed sign for a curve should be treated how in bad weather?
options: a:Reduce speed below the advisory limit when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.;b:Be ignored if you are comfortable driving faster.;c:Follow only when traffic is heavy.;d:Increase speed to maintain momentum.
note: Advisory speeds are for ideal conditions—reduce speed further when road or weather conditions are poor.

question: When preparing to change lanes you should not:
options: a:Fail to check for other drivers who might be moving into the same lane.,b:Check side and rearview mirrors.,c:Signal to indicate your intentions.,d:Ensure the lane is clear before entering.
note: Do not neglect checking for other drivers who may also be attempting to enter the same lane; always check mirrors, signal, and verify safety.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Red lines.,d:Blue lines.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate same-direction lanes.

question: In traffic, what is the safest speed choice relative to other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limits.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to stay ahead.,c:Drive much slower than traffic to be cautious.,d:Vary speed frequently to stay alert.
note: Driving with the flow of traffic (within posted limits) reduces the chance of conflicts and collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may proceed carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:
options: a:You are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.,b:You are speeding to clear the intersection quickly.,c:There are pedestrians crossing.,d:You intend to make a U-turn.
note: If you are already in the intersection when a steady yellow appears, continue through carefully; otherwise prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway safely from an on-ramp you should:
options: a:Signal, look for a gap in traffic, and merge at approximately the same speed as freeway traffic.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for cars to pull over.,c:Enter slowly and expect freeway traffic to yield.,d:Enter at any speed because entering traffic has the right-of-way.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match speeds and yield to existing freeway traffic while merging safely.

question: How does increasing your vehicle speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision, reducing your ability to detect hazards.,b:It increases your field of vision and awareness.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:Speed has no effect on vision.
note: Higher speeds narrow your field of vision and require greater alertness to detect hazards earlier.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Turn from your current lane without signaling.,d:Back up to position yourself for the turn.
note: Do not make last-minute turns; continue to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger.,b:When controlled by a stop sign.,c:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.,d:All of the above.
note: Stop when instructed by a flagger or stop sign and whenever crossing signals/gates indicate a train is approaching.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The vehicle's speed.,b:The condition of brakes and tires.,c:The pavement condition.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, brake/tire condition, and road surface condition.

question: What is a 'No zone' in relation to large vehicles?
options: a:The large blind spot areas around trucks where the truck driver cannot see you.,b:A designated no passing zone on highways.,c:A one-way traffic area on city streets.,d:A school bus loading area.
note: 'No zones' are the truck's blind spots; avoid lingering beside or close behind large vehicles where the driver cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; the vehicle on the left must yield.,b:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.,c:Both should proceed simultaneously without yielding.,d:Yield to the largest vehicle first.
note: At a simultaneous arrival, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: How does alcohol affect your abilities as it accumulates in your blood?
options: a:Makes you feel less confident.,b:Speeds up your reactions.,c:Slows down your reactions.,d:Improves coordination.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, increases overconfidence, and leads to more driving errors.

question: Many crashes are caused by drivers who:
options: a:Travel too fast for the current road conditions.,b:Consistently check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Yield the right-of-way appropriately.,d:Follow all traffic laws.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a common cause of crashes; adjust speed downward when conditions worsen.

question: How can you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,b:Honk frequently to alert others.,c:Drive only in the right lane.,d:Follow the car in front of you closely.
note: By watching far enough ahead and keeping a safe following distance you can anticipate hazards and avoid sudden emergency stops.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:Only when behind a motorcycle.,d:Never; keep the same distance at all times.
note: Increase following distance when a large vehicle blocks your vision, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or whenever you need more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to turn left at a green light but heavy oncoming traffic exists. What should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and wait for a gap in traffic to complete your left turn.;b:Wait in the center until oncoming traffic clears only if you have room and the light is green.;c:Proceed into the crosswalk to wait for a gap.;d:Make a U-turn instead.
note: If the light is green, you may enter the intersection when clear and then wait to complete your left turn when there is a safe gap; yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a street with multiple lanes traveling in your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The lane nearest to the lane you came from (the closest lane moving in your direction).,b:The far left lane always.,c:The middle lane only.,d:Any lane as long as you signal.
note: When turning into a multi-lane street, complete the turn into the lane nearest to the lane you came from and do not immediately change lanes.

question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?
options: a:Reach down and attempt to pull it up.,b:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Shift to park immediately.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to stop.
note: Keep your eyes on the road, shift into neutral, brake steadily, pull off when safe, and turn off the engine.

question: While backing, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely only on mirrors.,b:Rely exclusively on mirrors and sensors.,c:Open the driver's door and lean out to see.,d:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing.
note: When reversing, physically look over your shoulder through the rear window; mirrors and sensors are helpful but not a substitute.

question: What do pennant-shaped signs (sideways triangular) typically indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:Yield ahead.
note: A pennant-shaped sign usually marks a no passing zone; additional text on the sign will confirm this.

question: Approximately how far might a loaded tractor-trailer travel before stopping from 55 mph?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet.
note: Large commercial vehicles require much longer stopping distances than cars; a fully loaded tractor-trailer may need nearly 400 feet at 55 mph.

question: Car drivers should remember that large trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots and require extra room to maneuver and stop.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger cars.,c:Are as maneuverable as small cars in tight spaces.,d:Do not require extra following distance.
note: Trucks have bigger blind spots and need more room to turn and stop; avoid lingering beside or close behind them.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, you should:
options: a:Set the parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb.;b:Set the parking brake and keep front tires straight.;c:Set the parking brake and keep rear tires against the curb.;d:Leave the car in neutral to prevent rolling.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and turn wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop, yield to others, and proceed when safe.,b:Stop only if other vehicles are approaching.,c:Slow down and go without stopping.,d:Treat it like a circular green light.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping time.;b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.;c:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.;d:Change lanes frequently to find better traction.
note: Increase following distance on slippery roads to compensate for longer stopping distances and reduced traction.

question: What actions should you take when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Look and listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before gates lower.,c:Drive around a lowered gate if you can.
note: When nearing railroad tracks, look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Never go around lowered gates.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Release the gas to let the car slow before braking.,c:Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,d:All of the above.
note: Avoid abrupt stops; release the accelerator early and brake smoothly while signaling, and check mirrors.

question: If you see the driver ahead driving with one hand and talking to a passenger, you should:
options: a:Give that vehicle extra space because the driver may be inattentive.;b:Try to outdrive them.;c:Follow closely to monitor their behavior.;d:Honk to get their attention.
note: Distracted drivers have reduced safety margins—allow extra space to reduce collision risk.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:Work zones or construction areas.,b:Regulatory instructions.,c:School zones.,d:Service facilities.
note: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance activities and advise caution and possible changes ahead.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane indicate a crosswalk; as a driver, you should:
options: a:Motor vehicles have right-of-way.,b:Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.,c:No one has right-of-way.,d:Only yield when lights flash.
note: Marked crosswalks show where pedestrians cross; you must stop and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: If another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:
options: a:Tap your brakes gently, slow down, and let them pass.;b:Brake-check them to force them back.;c:Turn on high beams repeatedly to annoy them.;d:Speed up to put distance between you.
note: Lightly tapping brakes and slowing encourages the tailgater to pass; if that fails, pull over and let them by.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roadways is true?
options: a:Your tires become less effective at clearing water as speed increases.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,d:Wet roads improve braking.
note: Higher speeds reduce tire ability to displace water, increasing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.,b:School zones.,c:Construction work ahead.,d:Speed limits.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is usually a yield sign, meaning you must give right-of-way when appropriate.

question: If you're on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and continue.,c:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,d:Pull to the left and stop.
note: On a one-way street you must drive toward the nearest roadside and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you verify before passing on a multilane highway?
options: a:The passing lane is clear.,b:You're allowed to pass only on the right.,c:There is no oncoming traffic.,d:Your vehicle has priority.
note: Before changing lanes to pass, ensure the passing lane is clear and signal appropriately to indicate your lane change.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:Because they are likely to be blind and may not see or hear approaching traffic.,b:Because they are required to yield to vehicles.,c:Because they are traffic enforcement officials.,d:Because they signal vehicles to stop.
note: White canes or guide dogs indicate blindness; you must slow, yield, and be prepared to stop for their safety.

question: A solid white edge line that angles toward the left indicates:
options: a:The road will narrow ahead.;b:There is an intersection ahead.;c:A construction area is ahead.;d:You must turn left ahead.
note: An edge line that slants toward the road center warns the highway is narrowing ahead.

question: What does a green traffic arrow indicate when displayed for a turn lane?
options: a:Traffic in the lane must turn in the direction of the arrow and may proceed.,b:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.,c:The arrow only applies if accompanied by a circular green light.,d:The lane may go straight or turn.
note: A green arrow allows traffic in the indicated lane to turn in the direction shown and has the same authority as a circular green for that movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what is true about turning?
options: a:You may still turn in that direction but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must go straight only.,c:You retain exclusive right-of-way to turn without yielding.,d:You must wait for a yellow arrow before turning.
note: A solid green allows turns but you must yield to pedestrians and any oncoming traffic not yet cleared from the intersection.

question: Which is the correct sequence when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.,b:Check mirrors, change lanes, then signal.,c:Signal and immediately change lanes without checking mirrors.,d:Flash your headlights, then change lanes.
note: Signal in advance, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder to view the blind spot, and change lanes only when safe.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving tend to:
options: a:Have trouble staying in their lane and controlling their vehicle due to distraction.;b:Make no driving errors and perform better.;c:Drive faster and more safely.;d:Never become distracted by food or drink.
note: Eating and drinking distract from driving by requiring hands off the wheel and attention away from the road, increasing crash risk.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.,b:Turn the wheels toward the curb.,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,d:Turn wheels to the left only if facing west.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so a roll will move the vehicle into the curb, not into traffic.

question: A small vehicle may begin to float in approximately how much standing water?
options: a:Six inches of water.,b:Two inches of water.,c:One foot of water.,d:Three feet of water.
note: Small vehicles can begin to float in as little as six inches of standing water; avoid driving through flooded areas.

question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:
options: a:Require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles.;b:Require less stopping distance than cars.;c:Can turn in a smaller radius than most cars.;d:Are always easier to pass downhill.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles do.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive simultaneously and the other vehicle is to your right, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the other vehicle.;b:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.;c:Enter the intersection and force the other to stop.;d:Proceed since you arrived first.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on your right when arriving at the same time; the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Is smoking or preparing to smoke while driving distracting?
options: a:Yes — these are distracting activities.,b:No — they do not affect driving.,c:They help maintain alertness.,d:Only lighting a cigarette is distracting.
note: Smoking can distract you by taking your hands or eyes off the road and should be avoided while driving.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.,d:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle indicating a vehicle is traveling 25 mph or slower.

question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:
options: a:Obey all traffic signals, watch for trains, and look both ways before crossing tracks.,b:Assume trains always stop for cars.,c:Drive around lowered gates if no train appears.,d:Ignore traffic signals if a train is not visible.
note: Light rail vehicles follow signals and can share the roadway; always obey signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.

question: How should you respond when you see a school crossing sign?
options: a:Always come to a stop, even without a stop sign.,b:Be alert for children and be ready to stop.,c:Blow your horn whenever children are present.
note: When approaching a school crossing sign, be especially alert for children and be prepared to stop. Always yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk.

question: Traffic signs and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Obeyed at all times.;b:Followed only when other traffic is present.;c:Considered suggestions.;d:Ignored if inconvenient.
note: Traffic control devices direct traffic and must be obeyed to ensure safety and legal compliance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop at the stop line before any crosswalk or intersection.,b:Slow and proceed if no traffic is visible.,c:Yield to oncoming traffic only.,d:Turn right after stopping without checking for pedestrians.
note: A red light means stop before any stop line, crosswalk, or intersection and remain stopped until the signal changes.

question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks to be safe?
options: a:Look both ways and listen, then proceed only if safe.;b:Cross quickly when you see a train.;c:Only look when red lights are flashing.;d:Assume no train is coming on single-track crossings.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions and obey signals before crossing tracks; never proceed unless you are sure it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.;b:The exact speed you must travel to avoid a ticket under all conditions.;c:A recommended speed only for heavy vehicles.;d:The speed you should always drive regardless of weather.
note: Speed limits show the maximum legal speed for ideal conditions; you may need to drive slower when conditions are unfavorable.

question: If you must stop quickly and your vehicle lacks ABS, you should:
options: a:Firmly pump the brakes to avoid wheel lock-up while maintaining steering control.;b:Hold down the brake pedal without pumping.;c:Lightly tap the brakes repeatedly.;d:Shift into neutral and release the brake.
note: If you don't have ABS, pumping the brake pedal helps you stop quickly while retaining some steering control.

question: If you encounter an animal on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Pass the animal as closely as possible.,b:No special action is required.,c:Sound your horn continuously.,d:Pass slowly and cautiously to avoid startling it.
note: Slow down and pass animals cautiously to avoid startling them and causing unpredictable movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where no signs or signals indicate the rules, which vehicle has the right-of-way when two vehicles arrive simultaneously?
options: a:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,b:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car whose driver sounds the horn first has the right-of-way.,d:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: At similar roads without traffic control devices, a driver must yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.

question: When changing lanes to the left, how should you check your blind spot?
options: a:Glance over your left shoulder.,b:Look in your side mirror only.,c:Glance over your right shoulder.,d:Use only the rearview mirror.
note: To verify your left blind spot, briefly glance over your left shoulder before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:As far to the right side of the road as possible.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.,d:In the left-turn lane regardless of markings.
note: Prepare for a right turn by getting as far to the right side of the roadway as possible without leaving the pavement or bicycle lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down when exiting a highway?
options: a:After you have merged into the exit lane.;b:Before you enter the exit lane on the main road.;c:Only once you see the toll booth.;d:While still in the through lanes.
note: Move into the exit lane well in advance, and begin slowing down after you are in the exit lane, not from the mainline.

question: When driving near heavy trucks you should allow extra space because they:
options: a:Require increased stopping distance and have limited visibility.,b:Have decreased stopping distance and can stop quickly.,c:Produce less noise so you may not notice them.,d:Always drive faster than passenger cars.
note: Large vehicles need more stopping distance and have larger blind spots; keep a safe distance and avoid lingering beside them.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Slow down and drive more slowly than the posted limit if necessary.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit but with caution.,c:Increase speed slightly to avoid skidding.,d:Use cruise control to maintain traction.
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet; conditions may require driving below the posted limit for safety.

question: When you see other drivers acting angrily, how should you respond?
options: a:Don't make eye contact.,b:Don't gesture back.,c:Distance yourself from the situation.,d:All of the above.
note: Avoid eye contact and gestures; slow down or move away to remove yourself from potential danger.

question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside rearview mirror.,d:Use both inside and outside mirrors without turning your head.
note: Before every lane change, turn your head to directly check blind spots so that no vehicle is in the area you plan to move into.

question: If an oncoming car is to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you proceed?
options: a:Split the difference between them.,b:Let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.,c:Pull onto the shoulder to pass.,d:Pass the bicyclist first quickly.
note: Avoid dealing with two hazards at once — let the oncoming car pass, then give the bicyclist plenty of room to pass safely.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive immediately; emotions won't affect driving.;b:Calm and focus yourself before starting to drive.;c:Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.;d:Take a stimulant to stay alert.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and impair driving; take time to calm down and focus before operating a vehicle.

question: What can occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.;b:Their effects will always cancel each other out.;c:Nothing significant occurs.;d:The effects are always reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairing effects, causing greater impairment than either alone.

question: What risks do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:They can increase stopping distance and make turning harder.,b:They reduce the chance of hydroplaning.,c:They improve fuel efficiency.,d:They only matter in winter.
note: Worn tires increase stopping distances, reduce traction, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Which factors influence how alcohol affects a person?
options: a:Amount consumed, time between drinks, and body weight.,b:The color of the beverage only.,c:Whether the person has driven the vehicle before.,d:The brand of alcohol only.
note: BAC depends on how much you drink, how quickly, your weight, and whether you have eaten — these affect impairment.

question: How can you avoid drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Turn on your car radio.,b:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.,c:Slow down and drive more carefully.,d:Drink energy drinks and keep driving.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch; it's the most effective way to avoid drowsiness.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what must drivers of small vehicles be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises only.,b:Wind gusts that can affect vehicle stability.,c:Additional traffic signals.,d:Improved visibility.
note: Large vehicles can create strong air gusts that may push smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering.

question: To help prevent crashes, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Communicate your intentions to other road users by signaling and using lights or horn when appropriate.,b:Ignore other road users and trust they will see you.,c:Only drive on side streets where there is less traffic.,d:Avoid using turn signals to save battery.
note: Use signals, brake lights, horn, and eye contact when appropriate to make your intentions clear to others.

question: Pedestrians must follow which of the following rules?
options: a:Use crosswalks at intersections and obey Walk/Don't Walk signals.,b:Always yield to vehicles even in marked crosswalks.,c:Cross only when a vehicle stops for them, regardless of signals.,d:Walk against the flow of traffic on sidewalks.
note: Pedestrians should use crosswalks, look both ways, and obey pedestrian signals; drivers must yield to crossing pedestrians.

question: When stopped on an uphill incline, you should allow a larger space cushion in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:The vehicle ahead may roll backward when starting, risking a collision.,b:Traffic lights operate more slowly on hills.,c:You cannot see cross traffic from an incline.,d:Your brakes will not work uphill.
note: On an uphill stop, leaving extra space helps prevent being struck if the vehicle in front rolls back as traffic moves.

question: A good rule for passing other vehicles is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and legal.;b:Pass on the right whenever possible regardless of conditions.;c:Try to reach the front of slow traffic by passing repeatedly.;d:Always exceed the posted speed limit to pass quickly.
note: Passing increases collision risk—stay with traffic flow and pass only when safe, legal, and necessary.

question: What do round traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:An upcoming railroad crossing.,b:A school zone.,c:A no-passing zone.,d:A vehicle inspection area.
note: Round signs warn of railroad crossings ahead; exercise extra caution when approaching them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a Merging Traffic sign on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if it is safe.,b:Honk at the incoming traffic to warn them.,c:Always remain at your present speed.,d:Speed up aggressively to avoid merging conflicts.
note: On multi-lane roads make room for merging vehicles; change lanes if no one is beside you and it is safe to do so.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be dangerous, you must:
options: a:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed and it is safe to do so.,b:Slow down and proceed if you think you can beat the train.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk if no gates are down.,d:Drive around lowering gates if the road is clear.
note: Do not attempt to cross if a train is near; wait until it has passed and signals have cleared before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is room to pass safely on the right or when on a multilane roadway moving in the same direction.,b:When it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.,d:When there is no turn signal used by the vehicle ahead.
note: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left and there's a safe lane to pass in, or on multilane roads with two or more lanes in the same direction.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations and mistakes by other drivers.;b:It prevents other drivers from passing.;c:It keeps traffic flowing fast.;d:It reduces your fuel consumption significantly.
note: Keeping extra space around your vehicle provides time to react and reduces the chance of collisions from others' mistakes.

question: Regulatory signs primarily:
options: a:Indicate what a driver must or must not do (e.g., speed limits, no turns).,b:Are placed wherever there is a present danger only.,c:Are always diamond-shaped and yellow.,d:Warn of upcoming hazards only.
note: Regulatory signs tell road users legal requirements such as speed limits or prohibited movements and are often rectangular with black on white.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow centerline, what does this tell you?
options: a:You are entering a two-way road where passing is permitted when safe.,b:You are entering a one-way road.,c:The road is under construction.,d:You must always travel in the left lane.
note: A broken yellow line separates opposing traffic and allows passing when it is safe to do so.

question: If a driver behind you is driving aggressively, what should you do?
options: a:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,b:Speed up to challenge them.,c:Stare at the driver as they pass.,d:Brake-check to slow them down.
note: Move out of the aggressive driver's way and avoid eye contact or gestures that could escalate the situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you proceed when the traffic signal ahead is steady green?
options: a:Proceed but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light allows you to go but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to vehicles still in the intersection.

question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol impairs many skills needed for safe driving—reaction time, vision, coordination—and damages judgment, increasing risky behavior.

question: Before changing lanes on a highway you should:
options: a:Signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,b:Signal and immediately begin moving into the next lane.,c:Only check your mirrors and then change lanes.,d:Flash your headlights to alert other drivers and change lanes.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure safe driving afterward?
options: a:Drink coffee before driving.,b:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.,d:Eat a large meal to sober up.
note: Arrange a sober ride home; coffee, cold showers, or food won't lower your BAC or impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is parking expressly prohibited?
options: a:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,b:On a hill.,c:In a parking lot.,d:On private property with permission.
note: It is unlawful to park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes, among other restricted places; when parking on the street, stay within 12 inches of the curb.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control device?
options: a:A stop sign.;b:A yield sign.;c:A slow sign.;d:A no-entry sign.
note: A red flashing light requires a full stop and then proceed when safe, just like a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic (and always pedestrians and others already in the intersection).,b:Other drivers who are already in the intersection only.,c:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection only.,d:No one; left turns always have the right-of-way.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming traffic; you must also yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and anyone already in the intersection.

question: What is the primary purpose of a diamond-shaped traffic sign?
options: a:To warn of existing or potential hazards ahead.,b:To indicate mandatory regulatory rules.,c:To mark historical sites.,d:To identify parking areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs typically warn drivers of potential hazards or changing road conditions.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon.,b:Rectangle.,c:Circle.,d:Triangle.
note: The stop sign is uniquely eight-sided (an octagon) and always means stop.

question: Under ideal conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain behind the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Three to four seconds.,b:Two seconds.,c:Five to seven seconds.,d:Less than one second.
note: Maintain at least a three- to four-second following distance in good conditions; increase it when conditions worsen.

question: Which effect can alcohol have on a driver?
options: a:It slows your reaction time.,b:It gives you false confidence.,c:It impairs your thinking ability.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows reaction time, coordination, and judgment. It can also create false confidence and impair thinking, vision, and distance judgment.

question: Drowsy drivers are at risk because they can:
options: a:Drive so poorly they resemble a drunk driver and seriously increase crash risk.,b:Fully compensate by opening windows and turning up the radio.,c:Stay alert indefinitely by drinking coffee.,d:Reduce reaction times the same as sober drivers.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving similarly to alcohol; simple measures like coffee or open windows do not reliably prevent crashes.

question: When should you always use your turn signal?
options: a:Only when changing lanes on a highway.;b:When changing lanes, pulling into/out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area.;c:Only when another vehicle is nearby.;d:Only at night.
note: Use turn signals whenever changing lanes, parking maneuvers, or entering traffic from an alley/parking area to communicate your intentions to others.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.;b:You must come to a complete stop before turning.;c:You should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.;d:You have the right-of-way to turn left without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns but requires yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are first in line at a stop sign and the way is clear after the vehicles ahead pass, what must you do?
options: a:Stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.,b:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign.,d:Wait for a pedestrian signal.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:
options: a:Plan your trip in advance rather than rely solely on road signs.;b:Depend only on road signs to find your way.;c:Drive with only a general idea of your destination.;d:Ignore maps and rely on intuition.
note: Plan ahead when going to unfamiliar locations—check maps or routes beforehand instead of relying only on road signs while driving.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:Increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:Lessens the effect of alcohol.,d:Only increases sleepiness, not risk.
note: Combining drugs and alcohol increases impairment and the risk of a crash compared with alcohol alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does it mean when a driver's left arm is extended downward?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Turn right.,c:Slow or stop.
note: A left arm extended downward signals the driver’s intention to slow or stop. Adjust your driving if following a vehicle showing this signal.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Only parking lights.,d:Interior dome light for better view.
note: Low beams improve visibility in fog; high beams can reflect back and worsen visibility.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may not pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, gently apply the brakes, and when at a safe speed steer back onto the pavement.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,c:Slam on your brakes and stop.
note: If your vehicle leaves the pavement, remain calm, slow down gradually by gently braking, then steer back onto the road when it is safe. Do not make sharp turns to force the vehicle back onto the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to make them move.,b:Speed up and pass before they finish.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.,d:Ignore them since you have the green.
note: Yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if you have a green light; they always have the right-of-way in crosswalks.

question: How should you handle headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night?
options: a:Look straight ahead.,b:Look over your shoulder.,c:Look toward the right edge of the roadway ahead.
note: If oncoming headlights cause glare, look toward the right edge of the road ahead and avoid looking directly at the lights so you are not temporarily blinded.

question: What do two solid yellow lines down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed when safe.,d:One-way traffic only.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and mean passing is prohibited for drivers in both directions.

question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Roads are especially slippery just after rain begins.,b:Wet roads cannot cause hydroplaning.,c:You can stop in the same distance as on dry roads.,d:Use high beams for better visibility.
note: Wet roads are often most slippery just after rain begins; reduce speed and increase following distance to avoid hydroplaning.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal indicates that a ____ light will soon appear.
options: a:Flashing yellow.,b:Steady red.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing red.
note: A steady yellow means the signal is about to turn steady red — be prepared to stop.

question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in blind spots, you should:
options: a:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move before changing lanes.,b:Adjust rearview mirrors every minute, c:Honk continuously before changing lanes.,d:Rely only on automatic sensors.
note: A quick shoulder check helps confirm the blind spot is clear; do not rely solely on mirrors or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center markings show a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is beside your lane, you may:
options: a:Cross the lines to pass if oncoming traffic is clear.,b:Never cross the lines under any circumstance.,c:Only cross in emergencies.,d:Pass only during daylight hours.
note: If the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross to pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: Emergency vehicles generally:
options: a:Have the right-of-way when using sirens and/or flashing lights and you must yield to them.,b:Must always be followed closely by other cars.,c:Are not required to use sirens when responding to emergencies.,d:Cannot give instructions over loudspeakers.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or lights; follow instructions from them and avoid blocking their path.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Avoid speeding, maintain proper tire pressure, and replace tires with poor tread.,b:Drive at higher speed to cut through the water.,c:Use cruise control in heavy rain.,d:Drive with very low tire pressure to increase contact area.
note: Hydroplaning risk is reduced by slowing on wet roads and using tires with correct pressure and good tread.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if an intersection ahead is blocked by other traffic?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can fully pass through.,b:Enter the intersection and wait in the middle.,c:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves, even if you block the intersection.,d:Honk until the traffic clears.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; otherwise you may block cross traffic and cause a hazard.

question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic in that lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction.;b:Drivers may turn immediately without yielding.;c:The arrow is decorative and may be ignored.;d:You can proceed if no other cars are present.
note: A steady red arrow carries the same restriction as a circular red light: you must stop and may not turn in the indicated direction.

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is correct?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:A motorcycle with two riders is always more balanced than with one.,c:It is acceptable for other vehicles to follow motorcycles closely.,d:You may pass a motorcycle in the same lane it occupies.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane; you must be entirely in the adjacent lane before passing a motorcycle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering from a garage, alley, or driveway.;b:Only when you are on the main road.;c:Never when your signal is on.;d:Only at marked intersections.
note: Yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from a garage, alley, driveway, or similar location.

question: Alcohol commonly causes which of the following effects?
options: a:Loss of concentration, poor coordination, and slower judgment.;b:Improved coordination and faster reflexes.;c:Increased vision acuity.;d:Heightened alertness.
note: Alcohol impairs concentration, coordination, judgment, and other faculties necessary for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive first.,b:The driver to arrive last.,c:The driver who signals first.,d:The driver on the left when two arrive simultaneously.
note: Vehicles stop from all directions; the first to arrive proceeds first. If two arrive together, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

question: What is the single most effective action to reduce your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Stay in the right lane.,c:Limit driving to weekdays.,d:Drive slowly at all times.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce injury or death in a crash.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less than ideal driving conditions due to road work.,b:That it is summer.,c:That you must immediately stop and back up.,d:That a school is nearby.
note: Work zone signs (orange) warn drivers that road work or maintenance is present and to proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.,b:You are not required to stop at all.,c:Only after entering the intersecting roadway to get a better view.,d:At least 100 feet before the intersection.
note: Stop at the place nearest the intersection where you can see cross traffic without moving into the intersecting roadway.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate and quickly steer back on the road.,b:Take your foot off the accelerator, slow, and gently steer back when safe.,c:Stop immediately in the lane.,d:Turn on hazards and open the door.
note: Don't panic: ease off the gas, steer parallel to the road, slow, check traffic, then gently re-enter the pavement.
